Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 3a-c) reveal a hyperdense, metallic-attenuation foreign body within the right lower lobe bronchus causing obstruction and subsequent atelectasis/consolidation. The clinical history of hemiparesis suggests a predisposition to aspiration, and the progression of opacity and volume loss over time is characteristic of a retained foreign body leading to chronic post-obstructive changes.
